During the 1996–97 English football season, Chelsea competed in the [[FA Premier League]].

==Season summary==
With [[Glenn Hoddle]] leaving to become [[England national football team|England]] manager, Chelsea gave the managerial role to midfielder [[Ruud Gullit]]. Gullit would use his continental connections to bring in world-class international players such as [[France]] center-back [[Frank Leboeuf]], and [[Italy|Italian]] superstars such as midfielder [[Roberto Di Matteo]], Parma's playmaker [[Gianfranco Zola]] and the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] winning striker and [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] captain [[Gianluca Vialli]]. Gullit had a dream start to his managerial career as Chelsea won the [[FA Cup]] with a 2–0 win over [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], ending Chelsea's 26-year trophy drought and making him the first foreign manager and first black manager to win a major trophy with an English club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/ruud-gullit-leading-chelsea-to-triumph|title=Ruud Gullit - Leading Chelsea to triumph|website=Chelsea FC|date=3 October 2020|access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref>

Zola was voted [[FWA Footballer of the Year]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37417835/gianfranco-zola-says-chelsea-team-beat-eden-hazard|title=Gianfranco Zola says Chelsea 'team to beat' next year with Eden Hazard|website=ESPN|date=22 May 2015|access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref> after a brilliant first season at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] in which he scored 12 goals and contributed many assists, while fellow countryman and record £4.5 million signing Roberto Di Matteo scored one of Chelsea's goals in the triumphant Wembley final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/chelsea-cruelly-expose-boro-fault-lines-1262302.html|title=Chelsea cruelly expose Boro fault lines|website=Independent|date=19 May 1997|access-date=4 November 2025}}</ref>

The club suffered a tragedy in late October when director [[Matthew Harding]] was killed in a helicopter crash in [[Cheshire]] when returning home from the club's League Cup exit at [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Shaw|first1=Phil|title=Football mourns a true fan|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mourns-a-true-fan-1359957.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mourns-a-true-fan-1359957.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|work=The Independent|date=24 October 1996|access-date=10 September 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
